page: Microsoft Azure D128nlds_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine based on Intel processor architecture and managed under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Characterized as a network-optimized and low-memory variant, this instance provides 128 dedicated vCPUs along with 256.0 GB of system memory. This allocation corresponds to 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory configuration that favors high-density processor allocation over excessive memory capacity. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

A central physical feature of the D128nlds_v6 is its integrated local storage tier, comprising 7,559 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD capacity. In addition to this bundled local disk, the host supports Premium Storage attachments for persistent external volumes. While published benchmark metrics are not recorded for this specific profile, the presence of 128 dedicated cores coupled with direct NVMe disk storage ensures sustained multi-threaded execution and low-latency storage throughput for temporary data handling.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the reduced memory allocation lowers resource overhead relative to standard general-purpose profiles, delivering cost effectiveness for environments that saturate compute threads rather than RAM. The primary tradeoff lies in the memory constraint of 2.0 GB per thread, which is insufficient for large in-memory databases. Consequently, the instance is targeted toward compute-heavy batch processing, distributed build and compilation farms, large-scale ETL pipelines, video transcoding, and scientific modeling requiring rapid local caching.
description: Microsoft Azure D128nlds_v6 is an x86_64 instance powered by Intel processors and virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. Designed as a network-optimized, low-memory variant within its series, the instance supplies 128 dedicated vCPUs paired with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The configuration integrates a massive 7,559 GB NVMe SSD for fast local scratch and temporary storage, while retaining compatibility with Premium Storage. It contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. By pairing dense dedicated multi-core compute capability with substantial high-speed local disk capacity at a reduced memory ratio, the instance offers cost-efficient scaling for workloads that demand significant parallel processor execution and heavy local I/O without requiring large in-memory footprints. The architecture is suited for high-throughput batch processing, distributed compilation, video encoding, ETL pipelines, and compute-bound simulations relying on extensive local cache.
